[head=2][color=#e8b04b]Taypan[/color][/head]
Taypan is Crescent's principal contested commercial frontier. It has enough infrastructure to attract every major power and not enough uncontested authority to make any one of them sovereign in practice.
A convoy can cross an Imperial approach, berth under Gliessian neutrality, refit with Shinohara parts, buy intelligence through a Free Company broker, and meet a Pact caravan before leaving the same traffic network. Everyone needs access to something they do not fully control.
Power follows dependable bases and corridors rather than clean borders. A faction may dominate traffic without owning the space between lanes. A neutral station may depend on a foreign yard. A mining field can be militarily occupied for one Turning and exploited by somebody else in the next.
[head=3][color=#e8b04b]Crescent's political anchors[/color][/head]
- [bold]Domain[/bold] lies beyond Crescent. Crown legitimacy, high charters, Synod recognition, major appeals, and the election of the Kaiser come from its institutions, not from an admiral remotely commanding every Taypani patrol. - [bold]Asterwald and Edelheim[/bold] anchor Count Olywier's charter. Edelheim's court, archives, supply offices, schools, workshops, warehouses, estates, and religious houses turn the Count's seal into working government. - [bold]Chengridz[/bold] is the secure industrial and political rear of the Workers' Union in Crescent. It trains officers, manufactures equipment, receives refugees, preserves archives, and ratifies NCWL authority. - [bold]Porodschok[/bold] is known for technical institutes, medicine, research, and the specialists who staff laboratories, hospitals, shipyards, and calibration teams under many flags. - [bold]Malpais[/bold] is a hard industrial and logistical region shaped by mining, penal labor, armed unrest, salvage, refineries, smuggling, and populations wary of distant rulers. - [bold]Harbin[/bold] is a transit and logistics system of depots, relays, maintenance facilities, and freight schedules. Control shortens supply routes and makes war cheaper without deciding it by itself.
[head=3][color=#e8b04b]Why enemies still speak[/color][/head]
Taypan rewards safe conducts, paid escorts, hostage exchanges, neutral mediation, and contracts between governments officially at war. It is dangerous, but it is also one of the few places where enemies regularly have practical reasons to negotiate.
Gliess Santo survives by making neutrality useful. Prometheus and Tatsumoto extend Shinohara's industrial and commercial reach. NCWL bases connect the active front to secure Chengridz. Free Company yards keep a market open outside Shinohara control. Pact caravans use routes no large power can completely police.
